targetText: There is definitely no difference in principle between the phenomenon and the thing-in-itself, and there can be no such difference. The only difference is between what is known and what is not yet known
explanation: Lenin refutes Kantian agnosticism, asserting that human cognition can know objective reality itself; scientific discovery progressively transforms unknown things-in-themselves into fully understood things-for-us.

targetText: In the theory of knowledge, as in every other branch of science, we must think dialectically, that is, we must not regard our knowledge as ready-made and unalterable, but must determine how knowledge emerges from ignorance, how incomplete, inexact knowledge becomes more complete and more exact.
explanation: Lenin outlines the dialectical nature of reflection: human knowledge is not static or absolute at any single moment, but is an ongoing historical process of deepening approximation to objective reality.
